extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities (CCS project developers/operators), state and EPA permitting authorities, legal/regulatory reviewers, and stakeholders commenting on EPA power-sector CCS requirements
extracted.subtask_short: UIC Class VI permitting and CCS standards
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria and regulatory standards relevant to Class VI UIC permitting, CO2 transport/storage and related EPA determinations (BSER, cost, timelines, reporting) as discussed in the EPA preamble on power-sector CCS requirements. Covers permitting data submittals, modeling and monitoring expectations, statutory cost/BSER considerations, reporting, timelines, and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of review delineation (40 CFR 146.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 40 CFR 146.84(a), the area of review is the region surrounding the geologic sequestration project where USDWs may be endangered by the injection activity. The area of review is delineated using computational modeling that accounts for the physical and chemical properties of all phases of the injected carbon dioxide stream and is based on available site characterization, monitoring, and operational data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delineation must rely on computational modeling informed by site characterization, monitoring, and operational data; see EPA Class VI implementation materials and guidance referenced in the preamble (Implementation Manual, GSDT, Class VI permitting report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action for existing wells within area of review
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC permitting authorities may require corrective action for existing wells within the area of review to ensure protection of underground sources of drinking water (USDWs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting authorities should identify existing wells in the area of review and impose corrective actions as necessary to protect USDWs; see relevant UIC regulations and EPA Class VI guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seismic history and seismicity determination (40 CFR 146.82(a)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the permit applicant to submit and the permitting authority to consider information on the seismic history including the presence and depth of seismic sources and a determination that the seismicity would not interfere with containment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must document seismic history and evaluate whether seismic sources could affect containment; see EPA's 2018 Class VI Implementation Manual, EPA and NRC materials on induced seismicity, and GWPC induced seismicity guidance for technical/regulatory considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and Remedial Response Plan (40 CFR 146.94(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An Emergency and Remedial Response (ERR) Plan is required; see the 40 CFR 146.94(a) template referenced by EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EPA's ERR plan template and the Class VI implementation manual to prepare required emergency/remedial response procedures and information for permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confining zone requirement/definition (40 CFR 146.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Confining zone" means a geological formation, group of formations, or part of a formation that is capable of limiting fluid movement above an injection zone (40 CFR 146.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits and site characterizations must demonstrate the presence and integrity of confining zones capable of limiting upward fluid migration above injection zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on movement of fluids into USDWs (40 CFR 144.12(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory prohibition on the movement of fluid into underground sources of drinking water (40 CFR 144.12(b)); Class VI construction and operation requirements (e.g., 40 CFR 146.86(a)(1) and related provisions) and emergency/remedial response (146.94) implement this protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit conditions, construction and operational requirements, monitoring, and ERR plans must collectively ensure no movement of injec­tion fluids into USDWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class VI permit components to ensure USDW protection
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC regulations for Class VI wells authorize injection of CO2 for geologic sequestration while protecting human health by ensuring the protection of underground sources of drinking water; major components to be included in Class VI permits are described further in the preamble (section VII.C.1.a.i(D)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits should include the elements identified in EPA guidance (area of review, monitoring, mechanical integrity, confining zones, ERR plans, corrective actions, construction/operation standards); see EPA Final Class VI Guidance Documents and the Implementation Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice consideration in Class VI permitting and primacy
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA issued Environmental Justice Guidance for UIC Class VI Permitting and Primacy (2023) and related memoranda/letters to governors directing EJ considerations in Class VI decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting and primacy decisions should incorporate the EPA's 2023 EJ guidance and related agency direction; consult the August 2023 memo and accompanying materials for EJ analysis expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement for captured CO2 (GHG Reporting subparts RR/VV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities conducting CCS to comply with this rule would be required to send the captured CO2 to a facility that reports data under subpart RR or subpart VV (40 CFR part 98 reporting linkage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance pathways assume captured CO2 is sent to designated reporting facilities; see 40 CFR part 98 subparts and EPA GHG reporting rulemaking notices for reporting obligations and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER determination must consider statutory factors including cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA determines the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) based on considering information on statutory factors, including cost, on a source category or subcategory basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BSER analyses should document statutory-factor consideration (cost, energy, feasibility, etc.) and rely on transparent cost/performance analyses (see final TSDs).

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF flexibility for sources with fundamentally different costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a particular source's costs are fundamentally different from those EPA considered in making its BSER determination — making it unreasonable for that source to achieve the degree of emission limitation associated with implementing CCS with 90 percent capture — a state may provide a less stringent standard of performance (and/or longer compliance schedule, if applicable) for that source pursuant to the RULOF provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may use RULOF provisions to tailor standards or schedules for specific sources where source‑specific cost evidence demonstrates fundamental differences; see preamble section X.C.2 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of EPA extrapolation and "adequately demonstrated"/"achievable" standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Court precedent allows EPA to extrapolate from testing results to predict lower emissions rates, to forecast technological improvements allowing lower emissions or control at larger plants (where the agency has adequate knowledge), and to extrapolate effectiveness across related source types (Essex Chem. Corp.; Sierra Club v. Costle; Lignite Energy Council). The 'system' must be adequately demonstrated and the 'standard' must be achievable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory determinations can rely on reasonable extrapolations and lead-time considerations when supported by adequate technical evidence and case-law precedent; document the basis for extrapolation and available knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost analysis methodology and data sources (NETL baselines, TSD adjustments)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA and DOE/NETL cost and performance baselines (NETL Baseline Report, Cost and Performance Baseline documents, NETL CO2 storage cost model) are used for cost analyses; EPA adjusted NETL-reported costs to 2019 or 2022 dollars as appropriate and cites TSDs for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost reasonableness and method transparency require citing baseline reports, specifying year dollars and price deflators (e.g., GDP implicit price deflator), and referencing final TSDs and NETL documents for assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline assumptions and compliance date extension mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative timeline assumptions: pipeline feasibility 1 year, permitting 1.5 years, construction ~3 years (capture/pipeline/sequestration). EPA finalized a limited one‑year compliance date extension mechanism for certain circumstances to provide regulatory certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline and lead-time assumptions should be documented; applicants and states may rely on EPA's representative timeline when planning and may consider the limited one‑year extension mechanism where applicable (see preamble section X.C.1.d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce and resource assessment horizon (five-year assumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: For evaluating workforce and resources necessary for CCS installation, DOE's five-year assessment horizon (including about 3 years for construction activities) is considered reasonable by the EPA; EPA evaluated workforce and resource requirements over a five-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource and workforce planning studies should state the assessment horizon and justify assumptions; consult DOE workforce analyses and USEER for supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and primacy updates for Class VI permitting
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has increased transparency in the Class VI permitting process (e.g., publishing current projects under review, granting primacy to states such as Louisiana, and publishing lists of draft/final permits) and provides Class VI grant programs and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting stakeholders should consult EPA's public tracking tools, Class VI grants fact sheets, and primacy guidance to understand processes, available resources, and points of contact.
